estimand: Can a sequential generative match-state simulator improve the full 90-minute score distribution over an independent static Poisson baseline when both use the same chronologically available pre-match team information?

allowed_inputs: match identity and scheduled kickoff ordering
prior-match goal timing for state-transition estimation
forbidden_inputs: closing odds or any market data
B05 or any protected future labels

sample_identity_policy.chronological_grouping: match_date; all fixtures on the same date are predicted before any same-date outcomes are added to history
sample_identity_policy.fold_construction: remaining chronological match dates after burn-in are split into three contiguous folds by match count, without using labels

baseline.name: STATIC_INDEPENDENT_POISSON
baseline.pre_match_goal_intensity_source: rolling prior-match xG-for/xG-against with league home/away xG base rates
baseline.joint_distribution: independent Poisson home and away goals

candidate_catalog.name: WORLD_MODEL_V0_STATE_PATH
candidate_catalog.shared_latent_pace: one lognormal pace draw per simulated match; dispersion estimated only from prior-match total xG and clipped to a fixed range
candidate_catalog.state_feedback: home/away scoring hazards are multiplied by empirical-Bayes lead/draw/trail state multipliers estimated only from prior match goal timing

hyperparameter_policy.score_bucket: 0..7 plus 8+ independently for home and away

primary_metric.name: bucketed exact-score Log Score
primary_metric.delta_definition: candidate minus baseline; negative is better

secondary_metrics: natural Top-1 Draw calls and hits
stopping_rule: One frozen run. If the development gate fails, do not tune on these test labels; diagnose only and design a separately preregistered successor.
known_limitation: The open event feed is retrospective and its historical pre-match availability is not proven. Any positive result is research evidence only and cannot be a formal PIT claim.
